title: My Stomp Detection Broke Because Gravity Changed Velocity.y One Frame Later
author: Top-Cardiologist1011
selftext:
I hit a very dumb platformer bug that took longer to find than I want to admit.

Game context: [https://games.xgallery.online/forest-quest/](https://games.xgallery.online/forest-quest/)

The player could stomp a mushroom enemy, bounce upward, and still take damage immediately after. From the player's view it looked like: "I landed on top, why did I get hurt?"

The first version checked whether the player had just stomped by comparing vertical velocity.

Bad line:

const alreadyStomped = player.velocity.y === PLAYER\_CFG.stompImpulse

The logic sounded reasonable. On stomp, I set:

player.velocity.y = PLAYER\_CFG.stompImpulse

In my game that value is 8.

The problem was gravity.

Right after the stomp, the player update runs this line:

this.velocity.y -= cfg.gravity \* dt

With gravity at 25 and dt around 0.016, velocity goes from 8 to about 7.6 after one frame. So the equality check almost never survives long enough to protect the player from the next overlap check.

The fix was not to ask physics state a question it could not reliably answer. I added a tiny timer:

playerStompTimer = 0.15

Then enemy damage checks skip damage while that timer is above zero. It is long enough to cover the 2 or 3 frames where collision boxes still overlap, but short enough that the player cannot just walk through enemies.

The mushroom model was generated with Meshy, but the visual asset had nothing to do with the bug. The collision box, gravity order, and frame timing were the whole story.

This is one of those bugs where the code looks obvious until you remember the game loop is not a screenshot. Every system gets its turn, and one turn is enough to change the truth.
